subject: Linguistics
title: Garden Path Sentences
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Garden Path Sentences.

hook.text: 'The horse raced past the barn fell.' Read it again—it's actually a valid sentence.

buildup.text: Garden path sentences trick the parser into the wrong structure, then force a reanalysis.

discovery.text: 'Raced past the barn' is a reduced relative clause: 'The horse [that was] raced past the barn fell.'

twist.text: Psycholinguists use garden paths to study how the brain processes syntax in real time.

climax.text: These sentences reveal that parsing is incremental—we build structure word by word.

punchline.text: Your brain guesses the structure—and sometimes guesses wrong.

quiz.question: Why are garden path sentences hard to parse?
options: They lead you to the wrong initial structure
